section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Distributions
section_1.content: Briefly review that a 'distribution' is a shape showing how data spreads. Introduce the Normal Distribution (Bell Curve) as a predictable, symmetric baseline.
section_1.example: Visual: A histogram of students' heights forming a classic bell curve vs. a flat, uniform distribution of rolling a single fair 6-sided die.

section_2.title: The Problem: Non-Normal Reality
section_2.content: Explain that real-world data is often messy, skewed, or 'jagged.' Introduce the challenge: how can we predict outcomes if the underlying population isn't a perfect bell curve?
section_2.example: Visual: A 'Skewed' distribution representing the irregular waiting times for a bus throughout the day.

section_3.title: The Magic: Sampling and Aggregation
section_3.content: Define the mechanism: If we take many independent samples and calculate their 'Sample Means,' those means will behave differently than the original data.
section_3.example: Animation: 100 cute robots each picking 30 random jellybeans from a jar. They record the average weight of their sample. We collect all 100 averages.

section_4.title: The Core Revelation: Convergence to Normal
section_4.content: Present the CLT: As the sample size increases, the distribution of the sample means will always approach a Normal Distribution, regardless of the shape of the original population.
section_4.example: Visual: An animation showing a wild, jagged distribution morphing into a smooth, symmetric bell curve as the number of samples increases from 1 to 50.

section_5.title: Application: Why It Matters
section_5.content: Explain that CLT allows us to use standard statistical tests and confidence intervals even when we don't know the exact nature of the total population.
section_5.example: Scenario: A quality control manager at a toy factory tests small batches of robotic arms. Even if the defect rates in individual components are erratic, the average defect rate across batches allows her to predict overall factory performance reliably.
